sealed.statement: Schema provisioning survives its own idempotent retries during formation: a deterministic-intent replica-operation re-create whose zero-change collision lands on the prior attempt's durable row takes the idempotent EXISTING disposition instead of failing visibility it can never satisfy, an authoritative-not-confirmed collision outcome is classified transient (retry, never terminal FAILED poisoning later CREATEs of the same table), and the schema-job prologue honors the request deadline so a slow schema_operations partition yields an explicit pending/retry outcome instead of client-side silence — each proven red-first at the named race sites from the round-7 deterministic reproduction (local baseline repro plus archived runs 21-34-12 and 22-15-08), with the strict fail-closed collision contract preserved for non-intent creators in the sealed repository suites

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

hypothesis: Round-7 schema-provisioning race closures, all three at the named sites: (1) deterministic-intent creators (move.operationIntentId — schema jobs mint one id per job/target) request the idempotent EXISTING disposition on zero-change collisions instead of demanding fresh-timestamp visibility the prior attempt's durable row can never satisfy; the strict fail-closed collision contract is untouched for non-intent creators (sealed repository suite unchanged and green). (2) The authoritative-not-confirmed collision outcome joins the transient classification so the job retries instead of terminal-failing and poisoning every later CREATE of the same table via the schema_operations short-circuit; classifier exported for direct unit coverage. (3) The schema-job execute() arms its deadline race BEFORE the first await so insertOrAttach's un-deadlined gateway read/insert yields an explicit pending/retry outcome (provisioningDeadlineExpired) instead of client-side silence past the admin cap. Red-first: the new test file fails at base and passes with the candidate (6 assertions); query/rebalancer/control-plane globs at the pre-existing baselines (2/1/5); all static gates green.

claim: Independent verification approved the schema-provisioning collision-retry candidate 4fa4333f (three surgical fixes). Fix 1 was verified against the sealed strict contract: the newly-lenient disposition class is exactly the deterministic-intent creators (the schema-provisioning child intents and the legacy-target reconciler cleanup ids, both idempotent re-creates by construction; REPLACE intent-identity creators were already in the old condition), the pre-existing EXISTING-disposition handler attaches correctly for the schema case (no replace-intent assertion fires, intents are remembered, and maybeRearmReusedPendingOperation returns terminal rows as-is so a COMPLETED prior attempt is attached rather than rearmed), and the sealed repository collision suite is byte-untouched and green at 433 assertions, keeping fail-closed read-back for every non-intent creator. Fix 2 was verified by enumerating all three throwers of the not-confirmed message: the leader-cannot-see-durable-row case, the visibility-inequality case (which intent creators now bypass via the disposition lane), and the post-persist confirmation case are all durable-row visibility-timing outcomes where retry attaches on the next round; genuine divergence throws distinct non-transient messages (intent-hash conflict, replace-intent mismatch), divergence emits precede every return or throw so observability is preserved, and the classifier is schema-job-local so no other consumer's terminal semantics change; worst-case persistent failure degrades to an observable bounded retry loop instead of the old schema_operations terminal poisoning of every later CREATE. Fix 3 was verified for all three sub-attacks: the no-budget path returns the execution unchanged, Promise.race subscribes to both promises at arm time so a late prologue rejection is absorbed exactly as the pre-existing runJob race absorbed late rejections with no new unhandled-rejection class, insertOrAttach is attach-by-identity idempotent so late completion is harmless and the next client retry attaches, and buildOutcome's default branch on the synthetic PENDING workflow produces the documented pending/retry contract with defensive reason-code resolution. Red-first proven at BOTH levels: import-level at base plus a scratchpad behavioral probe showing the disposition-lane and deadline-race assertions fail against base source with the classifier import removed; the stub surface captures the real changed condition rather than neutering it. Byte-identical restore; 9 new assertions green; query glob at 146 of 148 with both failures reproduced base-identically; all static gates green including eslint on all three files; the quest harness runs its three declared guard files including the sealed repository suite through the shared never-self-certifying emitter.
